newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI - no comment on report Delors to be ECB chief.
newsitem.headline: EMI - no comment on report Delors to be ECB chief.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute on Wednesday declined comment on a German magazine report that European Commission President Jacques Delors would be the first president of the European Central Bank.

"This is a matter to be decided by political leaders, not by us," said a spokeswoman for the EMI, the forerunner to the European Central Bank which is scheduled to take control of monetary policy for the Euro region on January 1 1999.
In an advance summary of an article to be published Thursday, Wirtschaftswoche magazine said Delors was an ideal candidate to lead the ECB as he was highly regarded in Bonn and Paris.
Until now, Dutch central bank governor Wim Duisenberg, who is scheduled to replace Alexandre Lamfalussy as EMI president this July, was considered the frontrunner for the ECB post.

The EMI spokeswoman added that Duisenberg was considered a "favourite candidate" to be ECB president. Duisenberg had said he would be interested in the post at a press conference at the EMI last December.
But Wirtschaftswoche, without naming sources, said the choice of ECB head would be made by France, since Germany had won its fight to have the bank sited in Frankfurt.
French president Jacques Chirac was quoted as saying in December that the fact that Duisenberg would be the new EMI president did not mean he would automatically head the ECB.
Delors was travelling in Germany on Wednesday and could not be contacted.
An official at the Paris office of his Notre Europe foundation would say only: "This is the first time that we have heard talk of this."
Delors' age might work against him as a candidate for the ECB presidency -- he turns 74 in July 1999 and may be considered too old for the job.
Duisenberg, on the other hand, is 61 now and will turn 64 in July 1999.
